title: A hiring table at a bicycle repair shop
scenario: Spokewell Cycles (invented) repairs bicycles and sells each repair for \$4 in a perfectly competitive market. It hires mechanics in a perfectly competitive labor market at a wage of \$30 a day. The table shows the number of repairs it completes each day with different numbers of mechanics.

stimulus.title: Mechanics and repairs at Spokewell Cycles

table.caption: Repairs completed per day at the invented Spokewell Cycles (invented data for practice)

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Calculate the marginal revenue product of the third mechanic. Show your work.

rubric.point: \$40 a day, with work shown: MP = 34 - 24 = 10 repairs, and MRP = 10 × \$4

parts.sample: The third mechanic's marginal product is 34 - 24 = 10 repairs. MRP = MP × P = 10 × \$4 = \$40 a day.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Identify the mechanic with whom diminishing marginal returns begin.

rubric.point: The third mechanic: marginal product falls from 14 (second) to 10 (third)
accept: marginal product begins to fall with the third

parts.sample: Diminishing marginal returns begin with the third mechanic. Marginal product rises from 10 to 14 with the second mechanic, then falls to 10 with the third.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Identify the number of mechanics Spokewell hires to maximize profit.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Explain your answer to C(i) using marginal revenue product and marginal resource cost.

rubric.point: The third mechanic's MRP (\$40) is at least the MRC of \$30 (the wage), while the fourth mechanic's MRP (6 × \$4 = \$24) is less than \$30, so hiring stops at 3
accept: MRP of the 3rd = \$40 > \$30 and MRP of the 4th = \$24 < \$30

parts.sample: A profit-maximizing firm hires while MRP is at least MRC, and in a competitive labor market MRC equals the wage, \$30. The MRPs are \$40, \$56, \$40, \$24 and \$12. The third mechanic adds \$40, more than \$30, but the fourth adds only 6 × \$4 = \$24, less than \$30, so Spokewell hires 3.

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: The rent on Spokewell's shop rises by \$100 a week. Identify the effect on the number of mechanics it hires, and explain.

rubric.point: No change (still 3 mechanics), because rent is a fixed cost that changes neither any mechanic's MRP nor the MRC (the wage)
accept: the number hired stays the same because a fixed cost does not change MRP or MRC

parts.sample: Spokewell still hires 3 mechanics. Rent is a fixed cost: it is paid whatever the number of mechanics, so it changes neither the MRP of any mechanic nor the \$30 cost of hiring one more. The comparison of MRP with MRC, and so the hiring choice, is unchanged; only profit falls.
